nodes.label: sd is not a drop-in sed: it rewrites files in place by default
nodes.norm_label: sd is not a drop-in sed: it rewrites files in place by default
rationale: The three supporting rows were re-measured rather than assumed: in-place editing, first-match versus all-occurrences, and sed’s script language with no sd equivalent. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04198] A transparent `sed` → `sd` wrapper would silently turn every read-only command you type into a destructive file rewrite. `grep` → tgrep got away with a wrapper because search is side-effect-free; substitution is not.
[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04194] Confirmed — file went `a a a` → `X X X`

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04196] `2d`, `2q`, `y/ab/ba/`, `2i\`, `1!d` all work in sed; sd treats the whole thing as a literal pattern

nodes.label: A PATH shim for sed would be inherited by build systems, which call sed with -n, p and \1
nodes.norm_label: a path shim for sed would be inherited by build systems, which call sed with -n, p and \1
rationale: L4210 names the callers and the disqualifiers for the three call forms quoted at L4205-L4207. [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04202] I gave `grep` a **PATH shim** at `~/.local/bin/grep`, which every process inherits — build scripts included. That was safe only because the wrapper delegates anything risky back to GNU grep. For `sed` that same approach would be destructive, and this machine would actually hit it

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04210] Those are in your own `scripts/deploy/*.sh`, `scripts/ops/provision-vps.sh`, and `distribution/snipset-cli/install.sh`. cmake, autoconf, automake, and libtool are all installed, and CMake's own modules shell out to `sed`. None of those three forms survive translation to sd — `-n`, `p`, and `\1` alone rule it out. So `sed` stays reachable as `/usr/bin/sed` and only gets touched through `alias ssd='sd -p'` (preview, non-destructive) in interactive shells.
